name: code
description: code — coding-workflow plugin. Sub-skills for the manager/router engineering loop: `code:loop` drains a queue end-to-end (single ticket or many) with mindset-grounded autonomy and inline verification, `code:review` is one skill with three modes — session PRs by default, a deep cold review given PR number(s) (file:line grounding, architecture rubric, security pass), or a read-only whole-repo architecture-and-quality scan given `repo`/a path/`--since` — `code:learn` learns a codebase and writes durable navigation notes into the project's own AGENTS.md, folding a genuine coding-workflow lesson back into the plugin only secondarily. `/commit` splits the working tree into the maximum number of small logical commits. `code:review` spawns the repo's `code-reviewer` subagent (shipped from the top-level subagents/ layer, not from this plugin) for the non-author review. Publishing a distributable lives at the top-level `/release` command, not in this plugin. Also ships one self-contained command beyond the loop: `/code:prune` removes merged branches and worktrees behind hard data-loss guards (skips anything with uncommitted changes, stashes, unmerged commits, locks, or detached HEAD, using `git rev-list --count origin/$MAIN..HEAD == 0` as the load-bearing 'nothing to lose' check). `/code:clean` makes a codebase legible to agents and lands the cleanup: it reads the repo's docs as checkable claims and verifies each against the code, measures which files agents actually read and edit (fleet session index, not just git churn), censuses the user-facing surface for undocumented/untested/orphan entries, ranks six defect classes by agent-cost, and ships behavior-preserving PRs one concept at a time while recording a legibility scorecard so the trend is visible run over run.
